does: Dissolves sugar in water over heat and simmers it briefly to a clear, lightly thick liquid, which soaks into pastry, sweetens fruit and drinks, or glazes a cake.

intro.what: This syrup method dissolves sugar in water and lightly thickens it while keeping it clear.
intro.why: It teaches you to distinguish a pale syrup from caramel and anticipate thickening as it cools.

how: Put the sugar and the water in a saucepan, with a strip of lemon peel or a stick of cinnamon if the syrup is to be flavoured.
Stir over a gentle heat until every grain has dissolved, then stop stirring.
Bring to a boil and wipe down any crystals on the side of the pan with a wet brush.
Simmer until the liquid is clear and just thick enough to coat a spoon lightly. It thickens more as it cools, so stop early.
Add a little lemon juice near the end if the syrup is to keep, which stops it turning to crystals.
Let it cool to the heat the dish needs. Syrup poured onto pastry at the same heat leaves the pastry soggy, so one of them is cold.

cues.text: The liquid is clear, with no grains at the bottom, and the bubbles grow large and slow.
A cooled drop pressed between finger and thumb is sticky and draws out a short thread.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring after it boils, which throws sugar up the side of the pan and sets the whole pan to crystals.
mistakes.fix: Stir only until the sugar has dissolved, and wipe the side down with a wet brush.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling on until the syrup browns, which makes a caramel and not a syrup.
mistakes.fix: Take it off the heat while it is still clear and pale.

quiz.question: What distinguishes this syrup from caramel?
choices: It stays clear and pale instead of browning.
It develops a deep amber colour.
It has a deliberately toasted, bitter flavour.
quiz.because: This syrup is taken off the heat while pale; browning would turn it towards caramel.

quiz.question: When should you stop stirring the sugar and water?
choices: Only after the syrup has browned.
Keep stirring throughout the boiling stage.
quiz.because: Stirring after boiling can throw sugar onto the sides and encourage crystallisation.

quiz.question: What appearance shows the sugar has dissolved?
choices: White grains remaining beneath the liquid.
A cloudy mass of sugar crystals.
Clear liquid without grains at the bottom.
quiz.because: Clear liquid without grains shows the sugar has dissolved rather than remaining crystalline.

quiz.question: The syrup has become too thick after cooling. What would you change next time?
choices: Stop heating while it is still lightly thickened.
Boil until it is very thick while hot.
Wait for amber colour before stopping.
quiz.because: Syrup thickens further as it cools, so leave room for that change.
